question: Which of the following refers to the extent to which demand for a particular commodity decreases because others are also consuming the same commodity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Snob effect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Snob effect (स्नॉब प्रभाव) describes a situation where the demand for a good falls as more people consume it, because certain buyers seek exclusivity and want to be different from the crowd.

• It is a negative network externality — the individual's demand is inversely related to the total market demand for that commodity.

• Consumers exhibiting the snob effect prefer rare or unique goods and lose interest once the good becomes common.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The concept of Snob, Bandwagon and Veblen effects was formalised by economist Harvey Leibenstein in 1950.

• Snob goods are typically limited-edition or luxury items whose appeal lies in scarcity.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): The Demonstration effect refers to imitating the consumption patterns of others, not reducing demand.

• opt (Option 3): The Bandwagon effect is the opposite — demand rises because others are also consuming the good.

• opt (Option 4): The Veblen effect is when demand increases for a good because its high price signals status.

question: How does satellite imagery help in managing natural disasters in India?
option_1: By creating 3D video games of landscapes
option_2: By connecting people to mobile towers
option_4: By providing real-time data on floods, cyclones and droughts
solution_text:
The correct answer is By providing real-time data on floods, cyclones and droughts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Satellite imagery (उपग्रह चित्रण) provides near real-time data that helps in monitoring, early warning and management of disasters like floods, cyclones and droughts.

• Indian satellites such as INSAT and Cartosat series support disaster management by tracking weather systems and mapping affected areas.

• Remote sensing data enables authorities to plan evacuations, assess damage and allocate relief resources efficiently.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) under ISRO provides satellite-based inputs for disaster monitoring.

• The NDMA (National Disaster Management Authority) uses satellite data for coordinated disaster response.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Creating 3D video games is unrelated to disaster management.

• opt (Option 2): Connecting people to mobile towers is a telecom function, not a satellite imagery role.

• opt (Option 3): Tracking migratory birds is an ecological study, not disaster management.

question: In which year did Babur defeat Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1526 CE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The First Battle of Panipat (पानीपत की पहली लड़ाई) was fought on 21 April 1526 between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.

• Babur's victory marked the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India.

• Babur used gunpowder, field artillery and the Tulughma (flanking) tactic to defeat the larger Lodi army.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ibrahim Lodi was killed in the battle, ending the Lodi dynasty.

• The Second Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought between Akbar and Hemu, and the Third (1761) between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): 1519 CE was around the time of Babur's early raids into Punjab, not the Panipat battle.

• opt (Option 3): 1529 CE was the year of the Battle of Ghaghra.

• opt (Option 4): 1530 CE was the year of Babur's death.

question: Which government scheme aims to provide social security to workers in the unorganized sector?
option_1: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atal Pension Yojana (APY).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Atal Pension Yojana (अटल पेंशन योजना) was launched in 2015 to provide a guaranteed pension and social security primarily to workers in the unorganised sector.

• Subscribers receive a fixed monthly pension of Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000 after the age of 60, based on their contribution.

• It is administered by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Any Indian citizen aged 18 to 40 years with a bank account can join the scheme.

• The scheme replaced the earlier Swavalamban Yojana.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of wage employment, not pension-based social security.

• opt (Option 3): PMJDY is a financial inclusion scheme for bank accounts, not a pension scheme.

• opt (Option 4): NHM is a health-sector programme, not a social-security pension scheme.

question:
A ball is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of 10 m/s.
Ignoring air resistance, what is the maximum height it will reach?
(Assume g = 9.8 m/s²)
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.10 m.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Using the kinematic equation, maximum height (अधिकतम ऊँचाई) H = u² / 2g.

• Here u = 10 m/s and g = 9.8 m/s², so H = (10 × 10) / (2 × 9.8) = 100 / 19.6 ≈ 5.10 m.

• At the highest point the final velocity becomes zero, and gravity acts downward throughout the upward motion.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The time to reach the maximum height is t = u/g = 10/9.8 ≈ 1.02 s.

• The total time of flight (up and down) would be about 2.04 s.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): 1.02 m results from a wrong formula; 1.02 is actually the time in seconds, not the height.

• opt (Option 3): 10.2 m is obtained by dividing by g alone instead of 2g.

• opt (Option 4): 20.4 m is an incorrect doubled value, not the maximum height.

question: Which architectural style predominantly defines the churches of Old Goa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baroque and Manueline.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The churches of Old Goa are predominantly built in the Baroque and Manueline (बारोक और मैनुएलीन) styles brought by the Portuguese.

• The Basilica of Bom Jesus, which houses the mortal remains of St. Francis Xavier, is a famous example of Baroque architecture.

• The Churches and Convents of Goa were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Manueline style is a Portuguese late-Gothic style incorporating maritime and Renaissance elements.

• The Se Cathedral in Old Goa is one of the largest churches in Asia.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Indo-Saracenic style blends Indian and Islamic elements, seen in British-era buildings, not Goa's churches.

• opt (Option 2): Mughal architecture is associated with Islamic monuments in North India.

• opt (Option 4): Gothic Revival is a 19th-century European movement, not the defining style of Old Goa.

question: Which of the following complexes is also called a light-harvesting complex?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Antenna complex.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Antenna complex (एंटीना कॉम्प्लेक्स) is also called the light-harvesting complex because it captures light energy during photosynthesis.

• It consists of pigment molecules like chlorophyll and carotenoids that absorb photons and transfer the energy to the reaction centre.

• This complex maximises the efficiency of light absorption in the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The reaction centre converts the captured light energy into chemical energy.

• Photosystems I and II each contain their own antenna/light-harvesting complexes.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): The ATP synthase complex synthesises ATP; it does not harvest light.

• opt (Option 3): The ribosome complex is the site of protein synthesis.

• opt (Option 4): The spliceosome complex removes introns during RNA splicing.

question: On how many separate occasions has India been the country to organize the Asian Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Twice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India has hosted the Asian Games (एशियाई खेल) on two separate occasions, both in New Delhi.

• The first was the inaugural 1951 Asian Games, and the second was the 1982 Asian Games (IX Asiad).

• New Delhi is the only Indian city to have hosted the event.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The 1951 Asian Games were held from 4 to 11 March 1951 with 11 participating nations.

• The 1982 Asian Games introduced the mascot Appu, an elephant.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Once is incorrect, as India has hosted the Games twice.

• opt (Option 3): Three times is incorrect; India has not hosted the Games thrice.

• opt (Option 4): Four times is incorrect; India has hosted only two editions.

question: The Uniform Civil Code (UCC) primarily aims to:
option_3: Establish uniform laws on civil matters like marriage, divorce, inheritance
solution_text:
The correct answer is Establish uniform laws on civil matters like marriage, divorce, inheritance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Uniform Civil Code (समान नागरिक संहिता) aims to provide one common set of personal laws for all citizens, replacing religion-based personal laws.

• It covers civil matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance and adoption.

• It is mentioned in Article 44 of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Uttarakhand became the first state to implement a UCC in 2024–25.

• Goa already has a common civil code inherited from the Portuguese era.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The UCC deals with civil law, not criminal law.

• opt (Option 2): It does not aim to abolish parliamentary democracy.

• opt (Option 4): Regulating foreign trade is unrelated to the UCC.

question: Who is the Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities (NCM) in 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iqbal Singh Lalpura.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Iqbal Singh Lalpura (इकबाल सिंह लालपुरा) is the Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities (NCM) in 2025.

• He is a retired IPS officer and belongs to the Sikh community.

• The NCM was established under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The NCM works under the Ministry of Minority Affairs.

• Six communities — Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains and Parsis (Zoroastrians) — are notified as minorities.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Wajahat Habibullah was a former chairperson and India's first Chief Information Commissioner.

• opt (Option 3): Syed Ghayorul Hasan Rizvi has held other minority-related posts but is not the NCM chairperson in 2025.

• opt (Option 4): Zafar Sareshwala is a businessman, not the NCM chairperson.

question: In which state is the dance form 'Pandwani' performed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandvani (पंडवानी) is a folk singing and narrative art form of Chhattisgarh depicting tales from the Mahabharata, especially of the Pandavas.

• Teejan Bai is the most famous exponent of this art form and a Padma Vibhushan awardee.

• It is performed with the singer playing a tambura and narrating episodes with dramatic gestures.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pandvani has two styles of singing — Vedamati and Kapalik.

• Other artists like Ritu Verma have also popularised this tradition.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Madhya Pradesh is known for dances like Matki and Gangaur, not Pandvani.

• opt (Option 3): Jharkhand is associated with Chhau and Paika dances.

• opt (Option 4): Kerala is known for Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

question:
Consider the following statements with reference to mineral oil production in India.
1. Ankleshwar, Kalol, Mehsana and Kosamba are the important Mineral oil producing regions of Maharashtra.
2. Mineral oil deposits have been found in the Krishna-Godavari-Kaveri basin in South India.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are CORRECT?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 only.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ankleshwar, Kalol, Mehsana and Kosamba are important mineral oil (खनिज तेल) producing regions of Gujarat, not Maharashtra, so Statement 1 is incorrect.

• Mineral oil deposits have indeed been found in the Krishna-Godavari-Kaveri basin of South India, making Statement 2 correct.

• The Krishna-Godavari basin is one of India's most significant hydrocarbon-bearing basins.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Mumbai High (offshore Maharashtra) is India's largest oil-producing field.

• Digboi in Assam is the site of India's oldest oil refinery.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): '1 only' is wrong because Statement 1 mistakenly places Gujarat's oilfields in Maharashtra.

• opt (Option 3): 'Both 1 and 2' is wrong since Statement 1 is incorrect.

• opt (Option 4): 'Neither 1 nor 2' is wrong because Statement 2 is correct.

question:
Regarding the rural-urban linkages, which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?
1 Rural and urban regions are often in competition with each other.
2 Rural and urban regions are complementary to each other.
3 There is a continuous exchange of commodities between rural and urban areas through trade ties.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 and 3 only.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rural-urban linkages (ग्रामीण-शहरी संबंध) are essentially complementary, so Statement 2 is correct.

• There is a continuous flow of goods, services, people and capital between rural and urban areas through trade, making Statement 3 correct.

• Statement 1 is incorrect, as rural and urban regions are generally interdependent rather than in competition.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Rural areas supply raw materials, food and labour, while urban areas provide markets, technology and services.

• Strong rural-urban linkages promote balanced regional development.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): '1 and 3 only' is wrong because Statement 1 (competition) is incorrect.

• opt (Option 2): '1 and 2 only' is wrong for the same reason.

• opt (Option 4): '1, 2 and 3' is wrong because Statement 1 is incorrect.

question:
Consider the following statements.
1. At present, there are no active volcanoes in India.
2. The main cause of volcanic eruption is associated with plate tectonics, orogeny and sea-floor spreading processes.
Which of the above statements is/are CORRECT?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 only.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India does have an active volcano — Barren Island in the Andaman Sea — so Statement 1 is incorrect.

• The main cause of volcanic eruption (ज्वालामुखी विस्फोट) is linked to plate tectonics, orogeny and sea-floor spreading, making Statement 2 correct.

• Barren Island is the only confirmed active volcano in South Asia.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Volcanoes commonly occur along plate boundaries such as the 'Ring of Fire' in the Pacific.

• Narcondam Island in the Andamans is considered a dormant volcano.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): '1 only' is wrong because India has the active Barren Island volcano.

• opt (Option 3): 'Both 1 and 2' is wrong since Statement 1 is incorrect.

• opt (Option 4): 'None of these' is wrong because Statement 2 is correct.

question: In the Rigveda, what term is used for a collection of hymns?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Suktas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Rigveda, a collection of hymns is called a Sukta (सूक्त), meaning a well-recited or well-composed verse.

• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas and contains 1,028 suktas arranged in 10 mandalas (books).

• Each sukta is composed of several mantras or verses dedicated to various deities.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Rigveda belongs to the early Vedic period and is composed in Vedic Sanskrit.

• The Gayatri Mantra is found in the third mandala of the Rigveda.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Gayatri refers to a Vedic meter and a specific mantra, not a collection of hymns.

• opt (Option 2): Puranas are a distinct genre of later Hindu religious texts.

• opt (Option 4): Sutras are aphoristic texts, not collections of Rigvedic hymns.

question: In basketball, how many players usually make up each team on the court during official play?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In basketball (बास्केटबॉल), each team fields five players on the court during official play.

• The five positions are point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward and centre.

• A regulation game is governed by FIBA internationally and the NBA in the United States.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Basketball was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891.

• The sport made its Olympic debut at the 1936 Berlin Games.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): 7 players are not fielded per team in basketball.

• opt (Option 2): 6 is incorrect; a team has five players on court.

• opt (Option 3): 8 is incorrect for basketball court play.

question: What was one major provision introduced by the Pitt's India Act of 1784 concerning the Court of Directors?
option_1: It granted them authority to make laws for Indian states
option_2: It allowed them to dissolve Indian provincial courts
option_3: It made them accountable to the British Government in civil/military affairs.
option_4: It merged them with the Board of Control
solution_text:
The correct answer is It made them accountable to the British Government in civil/military affairs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pitt's India Act of 1784 (पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट 1784) established dual control over Indian affairs by the Company and the British Crown.

• It made the Court of Directors accountable to the British Government in matters of civil, military and revenue administration.

• It created a Board of Control to supervise the political affairs of the Company.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Act was introduced by British Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger.

• It rectified the defects of the Regulating Act of 1773.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The Act did not grant the Court of Directors authority to make laws for Indian states.

• opt (Option 2): It did not allow them to dissolve Indian provincial courts.

• opt (Option 4): It did not merge the Court of Directors with the Board of Control; both coexisted under dual control.

question: Who is the author of the book 'The Ocean of Churn'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanjeev Sanyal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sanjeev Sanyal (संजीव सान्याल) is the author of the book 'The Ocean of Churn: How the Indian Ocean Shaped Human History'.

• He is an economist and a member of the Prime Minister's Economic Advisory Council.

• The book explores the history of the Indian Ocean region and its role in global trade and civilisation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sanjeev Sanyal has also written 'Land of the Seven Rivers' and 'The Incredible History of India's Geography'.

• He previously served as the Principal Economic Adviser to the Government of India.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Tony Joseph wrote 'Early Indians'.

• opt (Option 3): Devdutt Pattanaik is known for mythology books like 'Jaya' and 'My Gita'.

• opt (Option 4): Rohan Mukherjee is not the author of this book.

question:
Which of the following is/are correct about the National Games in India?
1) Indian Olympic Games began in 1924 at Lahore due to efforts of Noehren and Buck.
2) Renamed as National Games in 1940 after the 10th edition in Delhi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 is correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Games (राष्ट्रीय खेल) trace their origin to the Indian Olympic Games first held in 1924 at Lahore through the efforts of Harry Crowe Buck and A.G. Noehren, so Statement 1 is correct.

• The games were renamed as the National Games of India in 1940, but this happened at the Bombay edition, not after the 10th edition in Delhi, so Statement 2 is incorrect.

• These games promote sporting talent across Indian states.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The National Games are organised by the Indian Olympic Association (IOA).

• Gujarat hosted the 36th National Games in 2022.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): 'Only 2 is correct' is wrong because Statement 1 is correct and Statement 2 has an error.

• opt (Option 3): 'Both 1 and 2 are correct' is wrong since Statement 2 is inaccurate.

• opt (Option 4): 'Neither 1 nor 2 are Correct' is wrong because Statement 1 is correct.

question: Which All-India Service is allotted to State cadres but controlled jointly by Centre and State?
solution_text:
The correct answer is IAS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Administrative Service (भारतीय प्रशासनिक सेवा) is an All-India Service whose officers are allotted to State cadres but controlled jointly by the Centre and the States.

• Officers serve both the Union and State governments during their careers.

• The three All-India Services are IAS, IPS (Indian Police Service) and IFoS (Indian Forest Service).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• All-India Services are provided for under Article 312 of the Constitution.

• The IAS was created in 1946 and succeeded the Indian Civil Service (ICS).

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): DSC (Defence Security Corps) is not an All-India Service.

• opt (Option 3): State PCS is a state-level service recruited by the State Public Service Commission.

• opt (Option 4): Indian Post is a central government department, not an All-India Service cadre.

question: Who was the prominent leader during the Quit India Movement, remembered for hoisting the Indian flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai in 1942?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aruna Asaf Ali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aruna Asaf Ali (अरुणा आसफ अली) hoisted the Indian National Congress flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay in 1942, launching the Quit India Movement.

• She is remembered as the 'Grand Old Lady of the Independence Movement'.

• She went underground to lead the movement and evade British arrest.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• She was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1997.

• Gowalia Tank Maidan is now known as August Kranti Maidan.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Sucheta Kriplani was a freedom fighter and India's first woman Chief Minister, but did not hoist the flag here.

• opt (Option 3): Annie Besant led the Home Rule Movement, not this event.

• opt (Option 4): Vijayalakshmi Pandit was a diplomat and the first woman President of the UN General Assembly.

question: The Green Revolution in its first phase (mid-1960s to mid-1970s) was largely ineffective in which of the following regions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Green Revolution (हरित क्रांति) in its first phase was largely ineffective in the eastern regions such as Bihar.

• The benefits were concentrated in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, which had assured irrigation and better infrastructure.

• Bihar lacked adequate irrigation, credit and input facilities during this phase.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Green Revolution was led by M.S. Swaminathan, known as the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'.

• It mainly boosted the production of wheat and rice through high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Punjab was one of the biggest beneficiaries of the Green Revolution.

• opt (Option 2): Tamil Nadu also benefited notably from the new agricultural technology.

• opt (Option 4): Haryana was a major gainer, especially in wheat production.

question: What does "P" in LPG reforms stand for?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Privatisation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the LPG reforms (एलपीजी सुधार), the 'P' stands for Privatisation, along with Liberalisation and Globalisation.

• These economic reforms were introduced in India in 1991 under Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.

• Privatisation refers to transferring ownership or management of public sector enterprises to the private sector.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The 1991 reforms were prompted by a severe balance of payments crisis.

• The New Economic Policy of 1991 opened the Indian economy to global markets.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Planning is unrelated to the abbreviation LPG in economic reforms.

• opt (Option 3): Production does not represent the 'P' in LPG reforms.

• opt (Option 4): Poverty is not part of the LPG reform terminology.

question: Aditya-L1 took how many days to reach L1?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 127.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aditya-L1 (आदित्य-L1) took 127 days to reach the Lagrange Point 1 (L1) of the Sun-Earth system.

• It was launched on 2 September 2023 and reached its halo orbit around L1 on 6 January 2024.

• L1 lies about 1.5 million km from Earth, allowing continuous observation of the Sun.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Aditya-L1 is India's first dedicated solar mission, launched by ISRO.

• It carries seven payloads to study the photosphere, chromosphere and corona of the Sun.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): 60 days is incorrect; the journey took 127 days.

• opt (Option 3): 200 days is incorrect for reaching L1.

• opt (Option 4): 365 days is incorrect; it did not take a full year.

question: Under which Article can the President promulgate Ordinances when Parliament is not in session, and how long do these last?
option_1: Article 123; until Parliament reconvenes or 6 weeks thereafter
option_2: Article 213; until next session of state legislature
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 123; until Parliament reconvenes or 6 weeks thereafter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 123 (अनुच्छेद 123), the President can promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session.

• An ordinance must be laid before both Houses when Parliament reassembles and ceases to operate six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament.

• It has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The ordinance-making power is an extraordinary legislative power of the executive.

• The landmark case D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar (1987) dealt with the re-promulgation of ordinances.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Article 213 empowers the Governor, not the President, to promulgate ordinances at the state level.

• opt (Option 3): Article 356 deals with President's Rule in a state, not ordinances.

• opt (Option 4): Article 352 relates to the proclamation of a national emergency.
